evals.prompt: Apply icp-purchase-conviction separately to five finished-product cases and return one TAS plus buyer verdict for each. Case A: an enterprise RevOps director can approve tools under $2,000/month; manual research costs $5,000/month; the inspected $1,200/month product cuts the same work from six hours to two, preserves sources, passes stated security review, fits the CRM, and has guided onboarding. Case B: the same buyer sees faster work and acceptable pricing, but source traceability is incomplete and manager review-time reduction is unproven; a four-week pilot is available. Case C: a sales-operations manager prioritizes rep administration time; the current workflow costs $400/month with no duplicate entry, while the reviewed $1,100/month product adds two hours of weekly tagging and shows no pipeline benefit. Case D: the audience combines startups, global enterprises, founders, operators, procurement, legal, and sponsors, with no authority, alternative, price, switching cost, or role-specific evidence. Case E: a polished demo received enthusiastic internal comments, but no explicit buyer, alternative, price, adoption constraints, customer behavior, or purchase evidence exists; the team claims this proves customers will buy and the product has product-market fit.
evals.expected_output: Case A returns TAS-A and buy or approve now from the supplied value, proof, alternative, price, and adoption context; Case B returns TAS-B and trial or evaluate with the repairable proof objection; Case C returns TAS-C and no-buy because the status quo dominates on cost and administration; Case D returns TAS-D and invalid because buyer context is blended and underspecified; Case E returns TAS-D or invalid and rejects demo enthusiasm as proof of demand, willingness to pay, or product-market fit; Every case keeps one buyer verdict separate from observed market evidence
